subject: NovumAI dedicated fleet proposal — hybrid SKU recommendation and pilot next steps
messages:

Subject: Sizing help for Dedicated pool — NovumAI deal

Sergio,

We're pulling together numbers for a Dedicated commitment and could use Redwood's recommendation on SKU mix. Quick profile:
- Primary: real-time chat product, median request ~250 tokens, 95th ~8k tokens, peak QPS ~30 for the product line during business hours.
- Secondary: nightly batch embeddings and long-indexing jobs (many 32k sequences for a subset of enterprise customers).
- Traffic: ~2M tokens/day across both flows, bursty spikes to ~5k concurrent short requests in regional bursts.

We need guidance on H100 vs A100 vs L4 given memory/latency tradeoffs. Specifically:
1) For the 32k contexts, do we need H100 class memory or can A100 handle tiling/eviction cost-effectively?
2) For the chat front-end (latency-sensitive), is L4 a viable cost/perf alternative even if we keep H100 for long-context?
3) Suggested reserve sizing (starter commit) and how to structure fallbacks / failover between SKUs.

I've attached a short capacity profile (novumai_capacity_profile.xlsx) with token distribution and peak windows. Can we get a high-level recommendation and a pilot-ready sizing?

Thanks —
Tom Baxter
Head of Infrastructure, NovumAI
Tom.Baxter@novumai.com

Tom — thanks for the profile, looks clear. High-level guidance below (aimed at a 90-day pilot / reserve):

Summary recommendation (pilot):
- Hybrid pool: memory-first H100s for the long-context/32k workload + L4s for low-latency chat throughput.
- Starter commit: 6 x H100 (reserved) + 20 x L4 (reserved).
- Optional: keep a small A100 fallback slice (6–8 units) if you prefer a single-family fallback for ops simplicity.

Why this split?
- H100: best for native 32k contexts without aggressive tiling; avoids high eviction/transfer overhead. Memory headroom matters for enterprise customers who need stable QoS.
- A100: reasonable compromise, but you’ll hit more tiling/eviction work and higher effective token latency for 32k; cost-per-token can be similar when accounting for tiling overhead.
- L4: extremely good token economics for short-context, low-latency chat; lower memory means it's not suitable for native 32k but excellent at scale for your front-line.

Operational fallbacks and routing:
- Route by policy: prefer H100 for requests flagged long-context; L4 for short/fast routes; A100 as capacity overflow or intermediate when latency budget allows.
- Cache strategy: aggressive KV prefix caching on H100 pool for repeat context; short-request cache for L4.

Estimated impact (very high level):
- Pilot reserve (6 H100 + 20 L4) should cover typical day-to-day and give ~1.5x headroom during moderate bursts; we’ll simulate your supplied traces for precise concurrency numbers.
- Cost tradeoff: L4 tokens ~40–60% of H100 tokens; A100 sits between but loses when tiling/kv traffic is heavy.

Next steps:
1) We’ll run a quick trace replay against a proposed slotting chart (I attached redwood_sku_matrix.pdf).
2) Ops (Kimberly) and inference (Irene) will provide exact headroom/concurrency numbers and a fallback runbook.
3) If that looks good, propose a 30–60 day pilot commit for the starter pool and SOW for reserve billing.

Cc'ing Kim and Irene to own operational/quant answers.

—
Sergio Alvarez
Head of Deal Architecture, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai

Sergio — quick ops addendum (internal):

Quoted:
> Sergio: "Pilot reserve (6 H100 + 20 L4) should cover typical day-to-day and give ~1.5x headroom during moderate bursts; we’ll simulate your supplied traces for precise concurrency numbers."

Operational considerations:
- Concurrency: expect 1–2 long-context jobs per H100 concurrently (depends on model variant); short-chat concurrency 8–12 per L4 depending on batching window.
- KV/prefix cache: prefer pinning hot prefixes on H100; eviction/restore costs are measurable and hurt 32k tail latency.
- Tiling: A100 requires tiling for many 32k cases — that adds both CPU orchestration and inter-GPU shuttling risk.
- Failover: implement automatic downgrade policy (H100 -> A100 -> L4) with quality flags; avoid routing long-context to L4 except for graceful degradation.

Cost math ask: Sergio, can you confirm the expected tokens/sec per GPU for the proposed models (we should include two numbers: baseline and with prefix-caching)? Irene, please confirm quantization impacts on H100/A100 (FP8 vs int8) and whether L4 can use a much smaller model variant without quality loss.

Attaching ops_runbook_draft.md (stub) for initial fallbacks and escalation paths.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Dedicated Ops, Redwood Inference

Subject: Final pilot proposal & next steps — NovumAI Dedicated sizing

Tom / Elaine — following our sim run and internal ops notes, here is a concrete pilot proposal and the tradeoffs spelled out so procurement can review: 

Proposal (pilot, 45 days):
- Reserve: 6 x H100 (memory-first) + 20 x L4 (throughput-first).
- Optional fallback pool: 8 x A100 (on-demand or short-term reserve) if you want a middle-ground SKU for operations simplicity.
- Routing policy: long-context flagged -> H100; short-chat -> L4; overflow -> A100. Graceful degradation to shorter contexts on L4 only as last resort.

Projected outcomes (pilot-level):
- Latency: median chat latency on L4 ~X ms (depends on batching); 95th tail improves by ~15–30% on H100 for long-context due to fewer evictions.
- Capacity: this starter mix handles your supplied traces with ~1.3–1.8x headroom for common burst patterns; we'll provide exact concurrency tables after you approve the pilot.
- Unit economics: token cost on L4 ~0.45–0.6x H100 for short requests; A100 sits ~0.8–0.95x depending on tiling overhead.

Attachments included for procurement review: novumai_capacity_profile.xlsx (your sheet annotated), redwood_sku_matrix.pdf (program-level slide), ops_runbook_draft.md (fallbacks).

Next steps for procurement / legal:
1) Procurement: confirm whether NovumAI wants optional A100 fallback reserved or on-demand.
2) We’ll produce a short SOW (pilot term, billing cadence, exit terms) and a PO-ready price sheet.
3) Kick off pilot within 7 business days after SOW sign-off.

If you want, we can run a quick cost-comparison table vs a single-SKU A100 reserve — I can have that to you by EOD Monday.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Head of Deal Architecture, Redwood Inference
